slides.title: Steganography
slides.teach: Read the source points, then explain the slide without looking. On Security+, recognition is not enough—you should be able to apply the concept to a scenario.

course.learn: Steganography hides the existence of information by embedding it inside another medium such as an image, audio file, or document. It is different from encryption, which hides meaning but not the existence of ciphertext.
course.why: Attackers can use steganography to conceal data exfiltration or malicious payloads; defenders may also use it for specialized legitimate purposes.
course.example: Secret text is embedded in the least-significant bits of image pixels so the picture looks unchanged to a viewer.
course.exam: Steganography = hide that a message exists. Encryption = make a visible message unreadable without a key.

slides.teach: Read the source points, then explain the slide without looking. On Security+, recognition is not enough—you should be able to apply the concept to a scenario.
defs: Replacing sensitive data with a non-sensitive token while the original value is stored separately.

course.learn: Tokenization replaces a sensitive value with a non-sensitive stand-in token. The original value is stored separately in a protected token vault or mapping system.
course.why: Applications can work with tokens without repeatedly exposing the underlying sensitive data.
course.example: A payment system stores a token such as TKN-83A9 instead of the real card number in the application database.
course.exam: Tokenization is not hashing: authorized systems may map the token back to the original value through the token service.

slides.title: Data Masking
points: Is also known as data obfuscation or data anonymization
Prevents the exposure of sensitive information

Data Masking
Is also known as data obfuscation or data anonymization
Protects the sensitive information
Prevents the exposure of sensitive information
slides.teach: Read the source points, then explain the slide without looking. On Security+, recognition is not enough—you should be able to apply the concept to a scenario.

course.learn: Data masking hides part or all of a sensitive value while preserving enough structure for a user or application to perform a task.
course.why: It reduces unnecessary exposure when full data is not required.
course.example: A support agent sees **** **** **** 1234 instead of the complete card number.
course.exam: Masked display with only part of the real value visible = masking. Replacing the value with an unrelated token = tokenization.
